causes.text: The rapid spread of the novel coronavirus triggered a worldwide market rout. As investors confronted the possibility of a global pandemic, more than $5 trillion was wiped off global stocks, and markets experienced their worst week since the 2008 financial crisis.

source_info.title: Coronavirus panic sent world share markets skidding again, wiping about $5 trillion off global stocks

effects.text: As the coronavirus crisis deepened, Alphabet's shares fell about 13% over March 2020. Investors feared that a pandemic-induced recession would slash advertising budgets and reduce Google's revenue, causing Alphabet's stock to track the steep decline in the S&P 500 despite a lack of company-specific bad news.

source_info.title: Why Alphabet stock fell 13% in March 2020

causal_reasoning_chain.description: On 2020-02-28, The emergence of COVID-19 disrupted economic activity worldwide, leading to steep losses across global stock markets.
Alphabet relies heavily on advertising revenue. Investors concluded that a pandemic-induced slowdown would cause advertisers to cut budgets, reducing Google's revenue.
On 2020-03-20, Consequently, Alphabet's share price fell in line with the broader market, declining about 13% even in the absence of negative company-specific news.

rationale: The pandemic shock created uncertainty about the durability of advertising revenue. Market participants punished advertising-dependent companies like Alphabet, anticipating a recession and weaker marketing budgets.
counterfactual_analysis: If COVID-19 had not become a global pandemic, advertising spending would likely have continued at normal levels, and Alphabet's share price would not have experienced such a steep decline.

adversarial_confounders.text: Simultaneous oil-price shocks and central-bank actions during March 2020 could also have influenced market behaviour.
adversarial_confounders.impact: These factors make it difficult to attribute the entire decline solely to pandemic fears.

details.commentary: A series of positive host and guest reviews reinforced trust in Airbnb's platform, encouraging more listings and bookings. This created a reinforcing loop where stronger network effects gradually translated into higher revenue growth and a supportive share price over subsequent quarters.
